title: A protocol to detect neurodegeneration in Drosophila melanogaster whole-brain mounts using advanced microscopy
protocol: Incapacitate flies using CO2.
Transfer flies to prelabelled Eppendorf tube, no more than 15-20 per tube.
Apply 1.8 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS-T and invert the tube several times.
Incubate tubes sideways at 20°C–23°C for 3 hours.
Wash flies 4 times with 1.8 mL of 0.5% PBS-T, each for 15 minutes with nutation.
Aspirate the top layer of liquid and replace with fresh 0.5% PBS-T during washing.
Dissect fly brains in 0.008% PBS-T.
Transfer dissected brains to Eppendorf containing 0.008% PBS-T.
Dissect fly brains and fix in 4% PFA for 20 minutes at 20°C–23°C with nutation.
Remove as much air sac as possible from the dissected fly brains.
Replace solutions within the Eppendorf containing fly brains carefully, allowing brains to sink each time.
Store fixed whole flies in 1× PBS at 4°C for up to several days before dissection if needed.
Dissect stored brains and store dissected brains in 1× PBS at 4°C for several days if needed.
Prepare phalloidin and DAPI cocktail in 0.5% PBS-T (580 μL per 600 μL Eppendorf).
Incubate tubes upright for 16–24 hours at 4°C with nutation after applying 400 μL phalloidin + DAPI cocktail.
Wash fly brains 4 times with 580 μL 0.5% PBS-T, 15 minutes each with nutation at 20°C–23°C.
Wash fly brains in 580 μL 1× PBS for 30 minutes with nutation at 20°C–23°C to remove residual detergent.
Mount fly brains anterior side up on Superfrost Plus microscope slides with SecureSealTM imaging spacer.
Cut a V-shaped wedge into the SecureSealTM imaging spacer.
Remove one adhesive layer of the spacer and apply it to the microscope slide.
Add 10 μL of SlowFadeTM Gold Antifade Mountant to the microscope slide.
Transfer brains in 1× PBS using a P-200 pipette with the tip cut.
Position fly brains at a 45° angle with anterior side facing up using a brush.
Aspirate residual mountant plus 1× PBS.
Allow brains to adhere for 10–15 min.
Add 30 μL of mountant on the top portion of the imaging spacer.
Angle the cover slip slightly.
Gently place the cover slip over the spacer and well containing the fly brains.
Allow the mountant to perfuse throughout the well and between the coverslip and spacer.
Avoid air bubbles during this process.
Seal the perimeter of the coverslip with nail polish.
Allow the nail polish to dry completely before storing or imaging.
Perform two-photon imaging of the vacuoles in the Drosophila whole-brain scanning.
Set the resolution to 1024 × 1024.
Set the Z-step to 1 μm.
Acquire approximately 150–180 Z-sections per brain.
Complete image acquisition for each brain within 8–10 minutes.
Maintain consistent laser strength and detection settings across all samples being compared during Drosophila whole-brain imaging.
Set scanning depth to cover the entirety of the adult Drosophila brain after mounting.
Adjust laser strength between 2–3% for sufficient signal intensity within the imaging setup.
Increase laser intensity for deeper layers in confocal imaging.
Adjust gain of the detector for depth-compensation imaging routine.
Use two-photon (2P) laser imaging for whole Drosophila brain penetration and uniform fluorescence generation.
Reduce Z-step for increased Z-resolution in 2P sectioning of the whole brain.
Store mounted slides at 4°C for several days to weeks before analysis.
Protect stored slides from light to minimize signal loss.
Perform whole-brain vacuole analysis using ImageJ.
Import a stack of images into Fiji (Image J).
Use the wand tool within Fiji to isolate vacuoles at their largest area and assign them as regions of interest (ROIs).
Adjust tolerance as needed within the tool to best select each vacuole.
Within the ROI manager, save each set of ROIs per brain as its own “.zip” file.
Select all ROIs per given brain and perform Measure with Area selected within Set Measurements.
Save Results as a “.csv” file.
Import measurement data within a preferred stats package.
